title: Log Transport (CU 732044)

chunks.heading: Description of Work
chunks.text: The Log Transport classification unit involves the transportation of logs from the cut–block to a log dump, dry land sort or secondary processing facility such as a mill by way of a logging truck. The following sections provide a description of the work that occurs.

chunks.heading: Planning
chunks.text:
During the planning phase, employers are responsible for ensuring truck drivers are adequately trained and have the appropriate credentials (e.g., air brake ticket, class 1, etc.). Employers are also responsible for ensuring that drivers receive orientation on the following topics:
• Weather conditions  Prime contractors and sub–contractors must ensure that, prior to arriving on site, all truck drivers are aware of the site specific wet weather shut down thresholds (water balance as determined by rain gauge readings)  This includes how and when the site will be shut down, who will communicate this information, and how it will be communicated
• Road use hazards, additional traffic and flow of traffic
• Location and grade of steep haul roads
• Ensuring hauling direction is suitable to existing road design
• Workplace rules and regulations for log landings, dry land sorts and mill yards
• Pick up/drop off locations

chunks.heading: Site Prep
chunks.text: Truck drivers are responsible for inspecting logging truck equipment daily including communication systems prior to the use or travel on a resource road(new requirement of 26.65 requires daily inspection of the cab guards and mounting system). Employers are also responsible for identifying all steep haul roads and ensuring risk assessments are conducted by a qualified person and ensuring the log truck drivers have been informed of the location and the hazards of the steep haul roads and the information, recommendations and instruction from the risk assessment (see OHSR 26.2 Guideline), and ensuring they have a qualified man check system and making themselves aware of the forest fire control plans.

chunks.heading: Loading Logs
chunks.text: If the logging truck is a conventional logging truck, meaning no self-loading capabilities, then the logs are loaded onto the truck by a log loader. If the logging truck is self-loading log truck then the truck driver in most cases loads the logs onto the truck. The hazards and controls depend then on the method of log loading.

chunks.heading: Transporting
chunks.text: Transporting the logs occurs in a variety of weather conditions, road type and grade (steepness of road) all of which affect the hazards and controls used.

chunks.heading: Unloading
chunks.text: As with log loading unloading can occur using a log loader if it is a conventional logging truck or by the truck driver if the truck is a self-loader. The hazards and controls depend then on the method used to unload the logs.

chunks.heading: Reloading Trailer
chunks.text: Reloading of the trailer onto the truck can occur via a number of ways (log transporter trailer hoists, mobile equipment, pre-load logging trucks). This depends on the unique operating characteristics of the worksite.

chunks.heading: Truck Maintenance
chunks.text: This section includes the regular maintenance of truck body, cab guards and tires while following proper lockout procedures for truck maintenance and proper procedures for tire servicing.

chunks.heading: Legislation
chunks.text:
The following sections of the OHSR capture the primary activities included in the Log Transport classification unit:
• OHSR Section 26.2, Planning and conducting a forestry operation
• WCA Sections 21–25

chunks.heading: Site Prep – Driver Orientation
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Inadequate orientation could result in driver not having clear instructions on truck configuration and workplace safety
Control: • Drivers are required to have a site specific orientation
Legislation: WCA Section 21, General duties of employers OHSR Section 3.23, Young or new worker orientation and training OHSR Section 26.2, Planning and conducting a forestry operation OHSR Section 26.5, Initial safety meeting

chunks.heading: Site Prep – Driver Orientation
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Inappropriate or non–use of seatbelt
Control: • Drivers are required by regulation and the law to wear seatbelts at all times
Legislation: OHSR Section 16.32, Provision OHSR Section 16.33, Use Motor Vehicle Act

chunks.heading: Site Prep – Inspection of truck equipment
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Unprepared for the work or upset condition
Control: • Pre–trip inspections
Legislation: OHSR Section 4.3, Safe machinery and equipment OHSR Section 16.34, Start of shift inspection OHSR Section 26.71.2, Daily log WCA Section 21, General duties of employers

chunks.heading: Site Prep – Inspection of truck equipment
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Truck backing up without alerting people in the vicinity
Control: • Truck is equipped with a backup alarm and backup lights
Legislation: OHSR Section 16.8, Warning signal device – backup alarm OHSR Section 16.9, Lights

chunks.heading: Site Prep – Inspection of truck equipment
chunks.text:
Hazard: • In the truck, the operator does not have clear vision
Control: • Windshields, side and rear windows, and rear–vision mirrors must be maintained
Legislation: OHSR Section 16.12, Maintenance

chunks.heading: Site Prep – Inspection of truck equipment
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Not maintaining a secure operators cab
• In the event of a collision or rollover drivers can be struck by loose tools or equipment
Control: • Maintain clean and secure cab
Legislation: OHSR Section 16.35, Securing tools and equipment OHSR Section 17.5, Securing equipment

chunks.heading: Site Prep – Inspection of truck equipment
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Welding grab hooks on cinches
• This practice can fatigue and weaken the cinch
• Operators can be struck by the cinch when they break
Control: • Do not weld on cinches
• There are now manufactured cinches with grab hooks installed
Legislation: OHSR Section 4.3(1)(i), Safe machinery and equipment

chunks.heading: Site Prep – Communication
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Truck is not equipped with the correct radio and/or radio channels for the roads being accessed
Control: • Ensuring radios are functioning (radio check)
• Ensuring radio channels are correct for the roads being accessed (radio check)
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.2, Planning and conducting a forestry operation

chunks.heading: Site Prep – Identifying steep haul roads
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Not identifying locations of potential hazards for drivers
Control: • Employers expected to be knowledgeable of all known hazards of the road system
Legislation: WCA Section 25, General duties of owners WCA Section 21, General duties of employers WCA Section 24, Coordination of multiple- employer workplaces OHSR Section 26.2, Planning and conducting a forestry operation

chunks.heading: Site Prep – Person check system
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Workers working alone
Control: • Develop person check system that will ensure drivers well being
Legislation: OHSR Section 4.20.2, Hazard identification, elimination and control OHSR Section 4.21, Procedures for checking well-being of worker

chunks.heading: Site Prep – Forest fire awareness and preparedness
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Unprepared workers in the event of a forest fire
Control: • Ensure workers are trained in the S100 training
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.3.1, Forestry operation fire fighting

chunks.heading: Loading – Self Loading Logging Trucks
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Drivers working alone and they in equipment that is unguarded
Control: • Person check system
• Safe work procedures (guarding)
• Safe guards on the loading equipment (boom deflectors, etc.)
Legislation: OHSR Section 4.21, Procedures for checking well-being of worker WCA Section 21, General duties of employers OHSR Section 26.13.1(1), Equipment operator protections OHSR Section 26.13.1(2), Equipment operator protections

chunks.heading: Loading – Self Loading Logging Trucks
chunks.text:
Control: • Log deck piles should be safe for the self-loading operators (i.e., should not exceed the height of the operators feet)
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.2, Planning and conducting a forestry operation

chunks.heading: Loading – Self Loading Logging Trucks
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Maintenance within self loaders often done at heights over 10 feet (log loader)
Control: • Fall protection
• Lockout procedures
Legislation: Safe work procedures WCA Section 21, General duties of employers

chunks.heading: Loading – Self Loading Logging Trucks
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Loss of stability of the tractor
Control: • Ensuring outriggers are placed as per manufacturer’s instructions and that they are well maintained and safe for use
Legislation: OHSR Section 4.3, Safe machinery and equipment

chunks.heading: Loading – Conventional Logging Trucks
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Exposure to mobile equipment
Control: • Driver orientation to the hazards of the landing
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.5, Initial safety meeting

chunks.heading: Loading – Conventional Logging Trucks
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Operator’s position during loading single or multiple bunks
Control: • Operator must not stand on the cab platform, or between the cab and a log being loaded
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.67, Load specifications

chunks.heading: Loading – Conventional Logging Trucks
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Suspended logs being passed over the driver and/or the driver’s cab
Control: • Safe work procedures and safe landing procedures
Legislation: WCA Section 21, General duties of employers OHSR Section 26.59, Suspended logs

chunks.heading: Loading – Conventional Logging Trucks
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Operator climbing on bunks to raise or lower stakes
Control: • Operator must not go on bunks and trailer assemblies
• If the operator must go on a bunk, they must be provided with a safe means to do so (i.e. a non-slip stationary work platform 20” wide, and the means for three points for contact)
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.66(4.1), Bunks and stakes OHSR Section 26.66(4.2), Bunks and stakes

chunks.heading: Loading – Conventional Logging Trucks
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Exposure to unstable logs on the load while attempting to secure the load with binders
Control: • Proper loading procedures and properly built loads (i.e. loads must be stable without the use of binders)
• Ensure safe work procedures are in place (as a number of recent injuries have occurred during this work process)
• The logs of the bottom tier and side rows must exceed beyond the front and rear bunks and stakes, according to the regulation
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.67, Load specifications

chunks.heading: Loading – Conventional Logging Trucks
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Significant MSI injuries from the application of binders without mechanical assistance (drivers throwing the binders over the load)
Control: • Unless it is not possible, use equipment or an alternate means of throwing the binder or pulling the binder over the load (using a ball and strawline rope)
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.68, Binders Safe work procedures OHSR Section 4.47, Risk identification OHSR Section 4.48, Risk assessment OHSR Section 4.51, Education and training OHSR Section 4.52, Evaluation

chunks.heading: Loading – Conventional Logging Trucks
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Temporary transport without binders (short duration to hammer)
Control: • Binders being applied to the load prior to leaving the landing and or the loader
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.68, Binders

chunks.heading: Loading – Conventional Logging Trucks
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Lack of communication between the truck driver and the loader operator
Control: • Proper signaling as per regulation and/or two way radio communication
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.67(1), Load specifications

chunks.heading: Transporting
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Loss of control due to physical impairment (hours of work)
Control: • Supervision
• Hours of work regulated for drivers by Provincial Legislation
• Log books required
Legislation: WCA Section 23, General duties of supervisors OHSR Section 4.19, Physical or mental impairment OHSR Section 26.71.2

chunks.heading: Transporting
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Loss of control due to substance abuse
Control: • Supervision
• Worker responsibility
Legislation: WCA Section 23, General duties of supervisors WCA Section 22, General duties of workers OHSR Section 4.20, Impairment by alcohol, drug or other substance

chunks.heading: Transporting
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Loss of control due to speed
Control: • Supervision
• Worker responsibility
• Motor Vehicle Act
• Forestry Act
Legislation: WCA Section 23, General duties of supervisors WCA Section 22, General duties of workers OHSR Section 4.20, Impairment by alcohol, drug or other substance No Jurisdiction No jurisdiction

chunks.heading: Transporting
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Loss of control due to weather
Control: • Supervision
• Worker responsibility to use proper equipment (i.e. chains)
Legislation: WCA Section 23, General duties of supervisors OHSR Section 26.2, Planning and conducting a forestry operation WCA Section 22, General duties of workers

chunks.heading: Transporting
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Loss of control due to steep haul roads
Control: • Employer required to conduct site specific risk assessments for steep haul roads
• Refer to OHSR 26.2 Guideline for further information
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.2, Planning and conducting a forestry operation

chunks.heading: Transporting
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Loss of control due to mechanical failure
Control: • Pre-trip inspections and timely maintenance and brake checks as required for the road
Legislation: OHSR Section 3.5, General requirement OHSR Section 3.9, Remedy without delay OHSR Section 4.3, Safe machinery and equipment

chunks.heading: Transporting
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Logs or chunks of logs sliding or rolling off the side of a log transporter while in transit
Control: • Ensuring at least two binders are used to secure the logs regardless of the height of the load
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.68(3), Binders

chunks.heading: Transporting
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Having inadequate cab guards (aluminum structure and anchor points)
• Cab guards provide the driver with life space in the event of a collision or sudden stop and are a critical safety element for log transport
Control: • Cab guards must meet the requirements of the regulation
• Frequent inspections of bull board/cab guard for damage and cracking at the anchor points
• Manufacturer’s instructions
• P.Eng. documents to certify load rating and main supporting structure is made of steel
• Certification by a P.Eng. that the main supporting structure is designed and constructed so that vibration and distortion generated by use cannot damage cab guard
• If full aluminum or hybrid (blend of steel and aluminum) load rating certification for vibration and distortion required
Legislation: OHSR 26.65, Cab guard OHS Guideline G-26.65(2)(e), Installing the cab guard on the log transporter in a manner acceptable to WorkSafeBC

chunks.heading: Note
chunks.text: Note: The off highway bull boards are now considered cab guards under the new regulation (definition)

chunks.heading: Unloading – Self Loading Logging Truck
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Drivers working alone and they are in equipment that is unguarded
• Loss of stability of the tractor
Control: • Person check system.
• Safe work procedures (guarding)
• Safe guards on the loading equipment (boom deflectors, etc.)
• Log deck piles should be safe for the self-loading operators (i.e. should not exceed the height of the operators feet)
• Ensuring outriggers are placed as per manufacturer’s instructions and that they are well maintained and safe for use
Legislation: OHSR Section 4.21, Procedures for checking well-being of worker WCA Section 21, General duties of employers OHSR Section 26.13.1(1), Equipment operator protections OHSR Section 26.13.1(2), Equipment operator protections OHSR Section 26.2, Planning and conducting a forestry operation OHSR Section 4.3, Safe machinery and equipment

chunks.heading: Unloading – Conventional Logging Truck
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Removing binders prior to the unloading the load (binder removal stations)
Control: • A load of logs must be restrained prior to the removal of binders
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.69(4)(b), Binder removal

chunks.heading: Unloading – Conventional Logging Truck
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Exposure to mobile equipment
Control: • Driver orientation to the workplace safety rules of the dry land sort or mill yard
• High visibility PPE
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.5, Initial safety meeting OHSR Section 26.7, Highly visible clothing

chunks.heading: Unloading – Conventional Logging Truck
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Suspended logs being passed over the driver and/or the driver’s cab
Control: • Safe work procedures and safe landing procedures
Legislation: WCA Section 21, General duties of employers OHSR Section 26.59, Suspended logs

chunks.heading: Unloading – Conventional Logging Truck
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Driver exposed to moving logs.
Control: • Drivers must not be exposed to moving logs during unloading
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.69(5)

chunks.heading: Unloading – Conventional Logging Truck
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Unsafe use of a binder removal station exposing drivers to unsecured loads
Control: • Safe work procedures
• Posted written procedures
• Station must be certified by professional engineer
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.69, Binder removal

chunks.heading: Unloading – Conventional Logging Truck
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Unsecured trailers
Control: • Empty trailers must be secured when loaded onto tractors
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.76, Securing trailers

chunks.heading: Reloading Trailers
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Suspended log truck trailer falling or becoming unstable
Control: • Safe work procedures for mobile equipment
• Annual inspections for log transporter hoists
Legislation: OHSR Section 26.2, Planning and conducting a forestry operation WCA Section 21, General duties of employers OHSR Section 14.14(g.1), Inspection and maintenance records

chunks.heading: Truck Maintenance
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Equipment not locked out during maintenance activities
Control: • Employer to ensure proper lockout procedures and safe work procedures are in place for maintenance activities on logging trucks
• Supervisors and workers to ensure lock out procedures are effective and are followed at all times
Legislation: WCA Section 21, General duties of employers

chunks.heading: Truck Maintenance
chunks.text:
Hazard: • Tire explosions
Control: • Following regulatory requirements for servicing multi piece rims
Legislation: OHSR Section 16.47, Training OHSR Section 16.48, Equipment and procedures

chunks.heading: Load Specification
chunks.text:
OHS Regulation: OHSR Section 26.67(1.3), Load specifications
Issue when…: • Observations of logs falling off of log trucks while in transit

chunks.heading: Load Specification (log rows)
chunks.text:
OHS Regulation: OHSR Section 26.67(3)(b), Load specifications
Issue when…: • Observation of a compensating reach type trailer where the loaded logs are less than 12 inches from the front and rear bunks and stakes

chunks.heading: Binders
chunks.text:
OHS Regulation: OHSR Section 26.68, Binders
Issue when…: • Observations of a loaded logging truck where the load is above the stakes and being transported without binders  Note: Log transporters are required to use binders to secure all log loads on the highway whether above or below the stakes

chunks.heading: Binder removal
chunks.text:
OHS Regulation: OHSR Section 26.69(4), Binder removal
Issue when…: • Observations determine a worker or driver is removing binders without the load being restrained

chunks.heading: Daily log
chunks.text:
OHS Regulation: OHSR Section 26.71.2(2), Daily log
Issue when…: • Observations during an inspection of a log transport driver reveal the individual does not have a daily log or has an incomplete daily log

chunks.heading: Warning devices
chunks.text:
OHS Regulation: OHSR Section 26.72, Warning devices
Issue when…: • Observations in a log landing determine that a log truck was backing into a loader with no distinct audible device

chunks.heading: Inadequate cab guard
chunks.text:
OHS Regulation: OHSR Section 26.65, Cab guard
Issue when…: • No certification or not mounted properly

chunks.heading: Cab guard
chunks.text:
OHS Regulation: OHSR Section 26.65(1)(b), Cab guard
Issue when…: • Observations of a log transporter where the bull board or cab guard is not as wide as the cab

chunks.heading: Damaged cab guard
chunks.text:
OHS Regulation: OHSR Section 26.65.6, Cab guard
Issue when…: • Observations of any damage to the cab guard such as, cracking/missing or broken pieces or corrosion

chunks.heading: Bunks and Stakes
chunks.text:
OHS Regulation: OHSR Section 26.66(7)(a), Bunks and stakes
Issue when…: • Observations determine that stake lines are being constructed with swaged wire rope

chunks.heading: Preparation
chunks.text:
• Bring and wear all appropriate PPE.  When climbing under the truck, wear safety eyewear.
• Ensure you have your two way radio and/or satellite phone on your person at all times.

chunks.heading: Arrival
chunks.text:
• Check in.
• Arrange for orientation to the cut block and/or dry land sort from worker or employer rep.
• Arrange for a worker or employer rep to accompany you during the inspection.

chunks.heading: Walk through
chunks.text:
• Obey all signage and workplace rules.
• Never approach any logging trucks without contacting the driver.
• Prior to a detailed inspection of a logging truck, ensure all loading activities have been stopped and the truck is shut down and secured for safe inspection.  Truck keys are in the officer’s pocket.  Wheel chocks are in place.
• Avoid inspecting log trucks while they are being unloaded.
• Do not conduct an inspection of a loaded logging truck unless the load is secure (i.e. binders).
• Never approach a logging truck that is being loaded on a steep slope, always keep a safe distance.
• Never try and overcome or flag down a logging truck (no jurisdiction to do so).
• Never ride in a logging truck.

chunks.heading: Wrap up
chunks.text:
• Communicate with employer/worker representative that the inspection is concluded and conduct exit meeting.
• Check out with employer.
